axis: By data flow (scan -> dedupe -> transcode -> sync), chosen because the repo has one pipeline photos move through end to end, and every file exists to serve one stage of it rather than a separate module boundary.

blocks.question: What is all this?
blocks.summary: A CLI that copies photos off a phone dump folder onto a home NAS, deduped and dated.
spool exists so that photos dumped from a phone reach the NAS deduped and dated without touching Lightroom.

refs.quote: spool exists so I never have to open Lightroom just to dedupe a phone dump.

blocks.summary: Everything past the scan stage assumes macOS; there is no Linux code path for transcoding.
New files land in the phone dump folder and come out as dated JPEGs on the NAS.
blocks.trigger: A file appears under ~/PhoneDump (SD card or phone USB mount).

stages.name: scan
stages.detail: Walks the dump folder for files newer than the last recorded run.

stages.name: dedupe
stages.detail: Hashes each file's content and drops anything already synced.

stages.name: transcode
stages.warn: Shells out to macOS `sips`; on Linux it silently copies the raw .heic through untouched instead of failing.

stages.name: sync
stages.detail: rsync over SSH into a YYYY/MM folder on the NAS.

blocks.output: Date-bucketed JPEG folders on the NAS, verified against a source hash log.

areas.name: Ingest
areas.blurb: Finds new files and reads local config.

files.role: Walks the dump folder for unseen files.
Loads NAS host, key path, and dump folder from ~/.spoolrc.

areas.name: Dedupe and transcode
areas.blurb: Content-hashes files and converts HEIC to JPEG before anything leaves the machine.

files.role: Content-hash dedupe against the local sync log.

areas.name: Delivery
areas.blurb: Gets bytes onto the NAS and records what shipped.

files.role: rsync over SSH into a dated NAS folder.
Entry point; wires the four stages together.

blocks.question: What did past-me decide and why?
blocks.summary: Two decisions still hold; one dedupe key was replaced after it caused silent overwrites.
Sync runs over SSH + rsync, not Synology's own cloud-sync client.
blocks.context: Synology Drive's cloud sync silently drops files over 2 GB.
blocks.decision: Shell out to rsync over an SSH keypair provisioned on the NAS.
blocks.consequence: One more moving part (SSH key management) in exchange for no silent drops.

refs.quote: we use rsync over SSH because Synology's cloud sync silently drops files over 2 GB

blocks.summary: Dedupe key switched from filename to content hash after phones with wrong clocks caused silent overwrites.
blocks.context: Filename + EXIF timestamp was the original dedupe key.
blocks.decision: Dedupe now hashes file content instead.
blocks.evidence: No commit message states the reason, but the code and history only make sense under this reading.
blocks.consequence: Slower dedupe pass on large dumps, but two files can no longer be silently treated as the same photo.
signals: dedupe.py imports hashlib and has no remaining reference to EXIF timestamps.
tests/test_dedupe.py asserts two files with identical names but different bytes are both kept.

blocks.summary: One dependency was added after the initial commit, a dated decision.
rows: Tried to replace the shelled-out sips call with native HEIC decode; partially reverted, see the transcode flow warning.

blocks.summary: Does the nightly sync still run from the Synology task scheduler, or did it move to a Pi?
blocks.why: install-nas-cron.sh assumes DSM's own scheduler, but a stray notes file suggests the job moved; nothing in the repo confirms which host runs it now.

guess.text: Probably moved to the Pi given the notes file, but unconfirmed.

blocks.question: Where is the sprawl?
blocks.summary: One dead file, one doc claiming a flag that no longer exists, and an unexplained size floor in dedupe.
This document was built from a1b2c3d; anything merged after that date isn't reflected.
legacy_uploader.py is dead: nothing imports it and the CLI it backed was removed.
docs/setup.md documents a --dry-run flag that cli.py no longer defines.

refs.quote: run with --dry-run to preview without writing to the NAS

blocks.summary: Why does dedupe.py skip files under 10 KB?
blocks.why: The size floor looks deliberate (a named constant, MIN_PHOTO_BYTES) but no commit message or comment explains the threshold, and it could be silently dropping legitimate screenshots.
